review_notes: I read the whole file and the base file's rncMap, rncExponent, coordinateExponent, rncMap_X, rncMap_C, rncMap_one and rncExponent_one declarations. The file's simp use is small and mostly simp only or simpa only with explicit lemma lists. I found no loop and no wrongly oriented rule. The one concrete issue is a private restatement of an existing @[simp] lemma, which the file then applies by hand. I also saw a redundant simp argument and an unfold of coordinateExponent in the same area. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour that I have not read from the sources.

findings.excerpt:
private theorem rncMap_one_eq_id (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    rncMap R 1 = RingHom.id (Target R) := by
findings.problem: The base file already has `@[simp] theorem rncMap_one : rncMap k 1 = RingHom.id (Target k)`, stated for any CommSemiring and so covering CommRing. The file adds a private copy of the same rewrite rule with a different name and reproves it, and the one use calls it by hand. A parallel unattached copy of a canonical simp lemma gives two names for one normal-form rule. It also means any other degree-one goal in this file has to be rewritten with the private lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `rncMap_one_eq_id`. Replace `rw [rncMap_one_eq_id]` at line 169 with `rw [rncMap_one]` or `simp only [rncMap_one]`, so the single canonical simp lemma is used. `RingHom.Flat.id` can then close the goal.
findings.benefit: The degree-one normal form is stated once, as the existing simp lemma. The file no longer carries a second copy of that lemma and its proof. If `rncMap_one` changes, the flatness proof follows it automatically.
